read.title: Read content
read.desc: Reading files, read-only commands, and fetching URLs you provided verbatim.

webAccess.title: Visit websites
webAccess.desc: Fetching or opening URLs Oru found on its own — the request sends the address and parameters to that site.

create.title: Create content
create.desc: Creating files, decks, and creating or editing Skills.

modify.title: Modify existing content
modify.desc: Editing, appending, moving, and renaming files (backstopped by real-time save and edit history).

overwrite.title: Overwrite existing content
overwrite.desc: Overwriting an existing file wholesale (including encoding conversion, with a separate irreversibility warning on the card).

fileDelete.title: Delete content
fileDelete.desc: Deleting an entire file (moved to the system Trash, recoverable).

sendExternal.title: Send content externally
sendExternal.desc: Sending content to people or external services via commands. On = never ask for any outbound send (careful); off = confirm per recipient.
sendExternal.tip: Why per-recipient by default: what you send can't be taken back, and the stakes depend on who receives it — a search engine gets your query, but an unknown address could get your files. Recipients you've confirmed are listed below and can be revoked individually; with the master switch on, even brand-new recipients won't be asked.

mcp.title: Change system environment · MCP
mcp.desc: Installing, upgrading, and removing MCP servers.

skillInstall.title: Change system environment · Skills
skillInstall.desc: Installing Skills (creating or editing a Skill is content authoring and is not asked).

scheduledTask.title: Create automated tasks
scheduledTask.desc: Creating, modifying, deleting, pausing, and resuming scheduled tasks.

destructiveCommand.title: Destructive commands
destructiveCommand.desc: Commands matching the destructive list: rm / mv / cp / sudo / kill / package installs / data-losing git operations.

dispatchSubagent.title: Dispatch subagents
dispatchSubagent.desc: Subagents inherit the current mode, and each of their own actions passes the gate separately.

catastrophic.title: Catastrophic commands
catastrophic.desc: rm -rf /, disk wiping, formatting — always asked, can never be authorized away.
catastrophic.tip: These commands can destroy the whole machine's data in an instant, so they're excluded from every "always allow" — each one requires your personal confirmation.

unknown.title: Unreadable commands
unknown.desc: Commands nested inside commands ($(…), eval, etc.) — Oru can't tell what they'll actually do.
unknown.tip: Technically: these can't be statically analyzed — their content is only known at runtime. When we can't tell, we assume the worst: asked every time by default. Turn on to skip the card even for unreadable commands.

noStructureGuarantee.title: File changes via the shell
noStructureGuarantee.desc: Deleting or changing files via the shell has no Trash and no overwrite protection, so it's always asked as a destructive command.
noStructureGuarantee.tip: The same deletion: the file tool moves it to the system Trash (recoverable); the shell (bash) removes it for good. The shell can't offer these protections, so file changes through it are escalated to destructive commands. This row is informational and follows the "Destructive commands" setting.

aiOwned.title: Overwriting Oru's own output
aiOwned.desc: Overwriting a file Oru produced and you haven't edited yet is not asked.
aiOwned.tip: How it's judged: the file's current content matches Oru's last written version verbatim, which counts as untouched. Change a single character and overwriting asks again. Turn off = ask even when overwriting Oru's own output.
